fact_text: Sweet Greens began in 2017 as a home kitchen business making salads, whose first batch of one salad, packed in six boxes, took the founder five to six hours to make.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: On the first day of retail the founder sold five salads from the first batch, which he took to sell in person at local outlets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: In the early model the founder did everything alone, from buying and washing vegetables to cutting and packing, then retailed the boxes himself.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The business's first customer worked at Unilever, and the founder built the customer base there gradually through word of mouth and repeat orders.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: In 2018 the business started meal subscriptions, offering calorie-counted meal plans that listed protein, carbohydrate and fat content for each option.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: A food blog post in Karachi led to an invitation from the owner of Sweet Greens, and the founder said he joined in 2019 despite having no experience and no money to invest.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: In 2019 the business opened a ghost kitchen, a delivery-only kitchen, funded with savings from earlier sales.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: In 2019 the business launched tacos, an idea the founder said came from a restaurateur friend who helped him.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The first taco batch was made at home by family and household staff with no employees and no sealing machine, so the tacos were sealed with a hair straightener.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: About 4,000 tacos sold out in one Sunday sale in 2019, and the founder said the product then went viral.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The menu grew because new items were introduced every month, and the founder later scaled the menu back down.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The business focused on delivery during the pandemic years 2020 to 2023, and the founder said COVID-19 effects were still felt through 2023.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The founder said he grew the business slowly because he lacked capital to open a restaurant at once, so he accumulated savings over several years before opening a dining space.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: After planning the kitchen layout, design and cleanliness standards, the business opened its first dining restaurant, which the founder said had been open about two months by Oct 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The founder argued that owner involvement in the food, rather than handing creativity to a chef, is what sets the brand apart from other restaurants.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The founder said consistency is the hardest part of running a restaurant, since food quality, portion size and pricing must all be right most of the time, and many operators break down over it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The founder's stated plan is to sell the concept across Pakistan first, starting with Karachi and then Lahore and other cities, before going international through a franchise model.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The founder said the company is building a supply chain that can deliver fresh produce consistently to outlets, and is considering sourcing directly from farms to stores to control costs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)

fact_text: The founder said restaurant operators in Pakistan face shortages such as water and gas, and that the sector has no level playing field, which leads many operators to give up.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'How Sweet Greens Went From Selling 4,000 Tacos to Opening a Restaurant | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-09)
